items.stem: A client asks whether an AI contract summary counts as legal advice they can rely on. What is correct?

options.text: No; AI output is support only and legal advice must come from a qualified lawyer
options.rationale: Correct: AI assists but cannot provide reliable legal advice or accept professional responsibility.

options.text: Yes, if the tool is advanced enough
options.rationale: Tool capability does not make output legal advice.

options.text: Yes, because the summary is in writing
options.rationale: Written form does not make something legal advice.

options.text: Only if the client agrees in advance
options.rationale: Client agreement cannot convert AI output into legal advice.

items.explanation: Correct: AI assists but cannot provide reliable legal advice or accept professional responsibility.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO risks are most specific to using AI on legal matters? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Loss of privilege if confidential material is entered into an uncontrolled tool
options.rationale: Correct: privilege and confidentiality are acute risks in legal AI use.

options.text: Fabricated case citations that look authentic
options.rationale: Correct: hallucinated citations are a well-documented legal-AI hazard.
A faster first draft is a benefit, not a risk.
Indexing is a benefit, not a legal risk.

items.explanation: Correct: privilege and confidentiality are acute risks in legal AI use.

items.stem: AI extracts a limitation-of-liability clause from a contract. What is the required next step before relying on it?

options.text: Verify the extracted clause against the actual contract text
options.rationale: Correct: AI extraction must be checked against the source before reliance.

options.text: Rely on the extraction without checking
options.rationale: Unverified extraction may be wrong or incomplete.

options.text: Assume the clause is standard and skip review
options.rationale: Assuming a standard clause risks missing a non-standard term.
The source must be retained for verification.

items.explanation: Correct: AI extraction must be checked against the source before reliance.
